summary: A Stage 1 registered report (accepted at ESEM 2026) from University of Southern Denmark, Oulu and Hawaii authors. It plans a large mining study: revert issues from the SQuaD dataset (450 OSS projects, 628k candidate issues, commits before 2021) to their pre-fix state, have an OpenCode agent with GLM-5, Qwen3.5-397b or Kimi K2.5 re-implement each fix, and compare agent and human commits on localization accuracy (package/class/method) and SonarQube/CodeScene/Understand maintainability and technical-debt metrics. Release-level 'counterfactual' TD trajectories are also planned. There are no results yet.

claims.claim: Agent localization accuracy will decrease at finer granularity (package > class > method).
claims.evidence: Stated as hypothesis H11 with a planned test; no data collected.

claims.claim: Agent-generated commits will introduce more TD than human commits and drive steeper TD growth across releases.
claims.evidence: Hypotheses H02b/H03 with planned Friedman/Wilcoxon/mixed-effects analyses; no results. The title ('AI Writes Code, Humans Pay the Debt') asserts the expected outcome before data exist.

claims.claim: Restricting to pre-2021 commits avoids contamination.
claims.evidence: It avoids AI-authored human baselines, but not the larger risk that the tested LLMs were trained on these Apache/Mozilla repos and their actual fix commits, which would inflate localization accuracy. This risk is not discussed.

patterns.note: Plans to use SonarQube/CodeScene/Understand static analysis as the TD measuring instrument for agent output; no evidence yet.
Localization measured via tree-sitter-java AST mapping and FQN normalisation.
Planned large-scale real-project (OSS) comparison of agent vs human fixes.

methodology.sample: Planned: SQuaD (450 projects, 63,586 releases, ~628k candidate issues), with stratified sampling expected for cost reasons; issues linked to commits via regex.
methodology.baselines: Human-implemented fix commits treated as a 'pragmatic' ground truth; divergent cases are to be manually sampled.
methodology.models: Planned: GLM-5, Qwen3.5-397b, Kimi K2.5 via a single OpenCode harness, chosen by median rank across three public leaderboards (March 2026).
methodology.variance: Not yet applicable; repeated-measures statistics planned. Repeated runs per issue are not specified.
methodology.ablations: Per-model sensitivity analysis planned; harness held fixed (acknowledged).
methodology.contamination_controls: Pre-2021 cutoff for human commits; no control for model training-data overlap with the target repos/fixes.
methodology.languages: Java-oriented (tree-sitter-java, Java 8-21, CK/JaSoMe), although SQuaD also contains C/C++ projects.

standards.peer_review: Accepted registered report (Stage 1) at ESEM 2026 per arXiv comment.
standards.artifacts: FAIR replication package on Zenodo promised; none yet.
standards.preregistration: Yes: Stage 1 registered report with hypotheses and analysis plan.

biases.detail: Protocol only; every finding is a hypothesis.
Pre-2021 OSS repos and fixes are likely in the LLMs' training data; this inflates localization accuracy and could make agent fixes resemble human ones.

Agent patches are only parse-checked (tree-sitter), not compiled or tested. TD would be compared between possibly incorrect agent patches and correct human ones, and the static-analysis proxies are not validated against developer-perceived debt (acknowledged).
The title presupposes the outcome the study is designed to test.
Only OpenCode as harness, acknowledged; results won't distinguish model from harness effects.
Release trajectories assume additive, independent per-issue metric deltas (acknowledged as a first-order approximation).

coi.affiliations: University of Southern Denmark (Coppola, Lenarduzzi), University of Oulu (Esposito), University of Hawaii (Kazman).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Planned: open-weight models GLM-5, Qwen3.5, Kimi K2.5; SonarQube/CodeScene as instruments. No vendor authors.
coi.funding: No acknowledgments or funding section found.
coi.detail: Academic authors. They reuse their own SQuaD dataset and earlier pipeline (Robredo et al.), a mild self-reliance rather than a commercial conflict.

verdict_reason: The pre-registered design is sound and relevant: Java, real OSS history, Sonar-family metrics, and a Stage 1 ESEM acceptance. But there are no results, so it carries no evidence. Agent patches are not functionally validated, and training-data contamination is unaddressed. Track it for the Stage 2 report rather than cite findings.
applicability: No findings yet, but the design is a ready-made template for the team's own measurement. Re-implement a sample of closed Jira issues from the several repositories with the team's agent hosts, then compare agent and human diffs with the local SonarQube instance (complexity, duplication, code smells, maintainability rating) and FQN-level localization. Unlike this protocol, also require the agent patch to compile and pass existing tests before comparing TD. That gives an internal, host-agnostic baseline for whether spec-driven agent changes add debt, measured with tools the team already runs. Do not use it to justify policy until the Stage 2 results exist.
